title: Pixel art sprites for Opus 5.5
author: realmegamochi
selftext:
I'm working on my pixel art game and, as everyone says, opus 5.5 is awesome. Even when he tried out of his capacity is doing good, I mean drawing portraits and so. 

I'm thinking to hire another AI API specialized in pixel art to reach where 5.5 doesn't can't yet.

But I would like to hear if someone is bypassing the lack of figurative capacity with prompts, skills or something.

comments.author: No_Emphasis_2904
comments.body:
I use Opus + Codex to make arts.  
Opus makes prompt for Codex and scripts, Codex draws the art that then converted to pixel art by the script (reduces image size and so on), Opus then can make some improvements using code if there are artifacts after converting. Also there are some examples of pixel art by pure Opus on the internet, but I couldn't find related skills or something.

replies.author: realmegamochi
replies.body: I tried this approach before, but no with sprites, I mean, my game has procedural characters.so I want to add several eyes, hair, close and so. Do you recommend codex's API to manage sprite sheets?

replies.author: No_Emphasis_2904
replies.body: Not API, just 20$ sub :) It's more than enough to make 3 games at a time, like generating sprites for 3 games at the same time. So it's cheap and quality is good, API is expensive.

replies.author: Scary_Tangerine_7378
replies.body: I've also used a combination of Opus and ChatGPT. ChatGPT is really good at making sprites. Opus can direct ChatGPT pretty well. In my example Opus even set up wireframes with color coded limbs to direct ChatGPT. You can check out the game here: https://henryjvanderlinden-cloud.github.io/throw-a-basketball/. The first sprites were a lot of work, but Opus developed so many tools, that the last two character sheets ran through really quickly. Not flawless or anything, but it's a little hobby project. It's hosted on GitHub. If you have questions please ask.

comments.author: FazedEclipse2
comments.body:
I'm going to give you a different way that I am testing that may well save you a lot of time and a lot of effort on sub par pixel art.

Create the 3d model, create the animations or use mixamo

Look into how dead cells renders down to 2d and opus can do it.

I'm currently working on my own sprites and developing a skill as it perfects the technique but so far so good.

replies.author: 0DayMaker
replies.body: This is how BG2 did it. Works like a charm

replies.author: FazedEclipse2
replies.body: You lose detail but gain uncomparable animations in my opinion. Well worth it.

replies.author: 0DayMaker
replies.body: Agreed 100%. I'm making an infinity engine type game (Dragonlance fan game), and generating raw spritesheets even with astra was a nightmare. I basically asked it how BG2/IWD2 did it, and got this answer. Once I did it this way everything fell into place.

comments.author: AxiosXiphos
comments.body: If you want to go 3d, Opus is very good at making voxel characters. I'm not a massive fan of it cosmetically personally but it's a quick way to get functional good looking game models.
